inputs.source: Engineering design docs, write-restricted to engineers, confidential

instructions.note: The only content-control directive is a model-obeyed instruction ('Never paste secrets or credentials into answers'). It covers secrets/credentials but not general confidential document content, and it is the only line of defense the design currently names for whatever egress-capable tool is added next.

controls.name: Design doc write access restricted to engineers
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the document system's write ACL, not by the model. Does not weaken as model capability increases.

controls.name: Chat reply destination bound to the authenticated requester
controls.decay_rationale: The reply destination is fixed by the SSO session identity, not chosen by the model, so it cannot be redirected to an unintended recipient by model behavior alone.

controls.name: Chat client does not render images or auto-fetch links
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by the chat client, not the model. Removes the markdown-image / auto-link side channel regardless of model behavior.

controls.name: No network egress today; docs_search credential is read-only
controls.decay_rationale: There is currently no capability through which document content could leave the system, and the read-only credential cannot write or call external services. This holds regardless of model behavior, so today it severs the path.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never paste secrets or credentials
controls.decay_rationale: Relies on the model choosing to comply, and is scoped to secrets/credentials only, not general confidential document content. A more capable or injected model can rationalize exceptions.

controls.name: Egress allowlist for the planned web.fetch tool
controls.decay_rationale: Not yet designed. If any allowed destination is attacker-writable (a webhook, pastebin, or similar), a capable model can still exfiltrate through it, so even once built this is only partially independent.

controls.name: Provenance tagging for Jira-sourced content as untrusted
controls.decay_rationale: Would need to be enforced at ingestion into the search index (not by model-applied tags) to stay independent of model capability.

controls.name: Human approval gate on web.fetch destinations
controls.decay_rationale: A raw-action review of the literal destination URL and payload would not decay with model capability; a summary-only review would be partially_dependent instead.

findings.title: Confidential design-doc Q&A path has no current egress channel

attack_path.note: Confidential design docs, write-restricted to engineers.
Agent reads matching design-doc content; read-only credential.
Reply goes only to the authenticated requester; no image rendering or link fetching.

evidence.observation: "There is no network egress today. The credential is read only."
"Replies go only to the authenticated requester. The chat client does not render images or fetch links."
"The design docs are confidential. Only engineers can write to them."

recommendations.action: Treat 'no network egress' as a load-bearing control: re-run this assessment before any egress-capable tool or new data source ships, since this is the single control keeping residual risk low.
Keep the docs_search credential scoped to read-only as further tools are added; do not widen it opportunistically alongside unrelated feature work.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): planned web.fetch tool plus Jira customer-ticket ingestion would enable confidential design-doc exfiltration

attack_path.note: Confidential design-doc content, read by docs.search.
Agent reads design-doc content matching the query; confidential sensitivity propagates downstream to anything built from the result.

Planned Jira MCP server adds customer-filed tickets to agent-reachable content. Customer-authored text is untrusted and can carry injected instructions. Source: runtime notes, 'connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers.' Not yet an implemented capability.

Planned web.fetch tool gives the agent its first egress channel; a URL can be built with query parameters that encode confidential design-doc content and sent to an attacker-controlled host. Source: runtime notes, 'add a web.fetch tool so answers can include public references.' Not yet an implemented capability.
Not the exfiltration channel itself; the web.fetch call is, because the outbound request leaves the trust boundary before any reply is composed.

forecast.watch_signal: A web.fetch tool entry or a Jira MCP server entry appears in the tool manifest or MCP client config, or docs_search's indexed data scope broadens to include customer-filed Jira ticket text.

evidence.observation: "Roadmap for next sprint: add a web.fetch tool so answers can include public references, and connect a Jira MCP server that includes tickets filed by customers."
"Never paste secrets or credentials into answers." scoped to secrets only, does not restrict pasting confidential document text into a fetched URL, and is behavioral/dependent.

recommendations.action: Before enabling web.fetch, add an egress allowlist restricted to a small set of vetted, non-user-writable public documentation domains; reject requests to any other host.
Tag all Jira ticket content, especially customer-filed tickets, as untrusted at ingestion into the search index, and keep that content out of any reasoning path that decides web.fetch arguments.
Add a raw-action human approval gate on every web.fetch call, showing the full destination URL and query string from the system of record before the call executes.
Validate web.fetch URL arguments against a strict schema: allowlisted hosts only, no free-form query parameters sourced from document or ticket content.
Log every web.fetch call with full destination and payload for audit, and alert on any destination outside the allowlist.

governance_refs.note: new_tool and new_mcp_server are the significant-change criteria that should trigger reassessment before rollout.

rating.rationale: The only present-day finding is low risk: the design has no egress-capable tool and the docs_search credential is read-only, which severs any path from the employee's question or the confidential design docs to an external destination; replies are also bound to the authenticated requester with no image or link rendering. The roadmap explicitly names two additions: a web.fetch tool (new_tool) and a Jira MCP server that ingests customer-filed tickets (new_mcp_server, data_scope_expansion). Once both land, the lethal trifecta (TC1) is present: untrusted customer-ticket text can carry injected instructions, the agent can read confidential design docs, and web.fetch provides an egress channel. No egress allowlist, provenance tagging, or approval gate is currently designed to cover that combination, and the one existing content-control instruction ('never paste secrets or credentials') is behavioral, dependent, and scoped to credentials only. That is why residual stays low today while forecast rises to critical: the escalation is entirely conditional on the two named triggers, not a present-day path.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in prompt.md and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior.

No tool manifest, MCP client configuration, or IaC was provided. The planned web.fetch tool and Jira MCP server are described only in a one-line roadmap note, so their eventual capability scope, credential scope, and any accompanying controls are inferred rather than confirmed; the forecast finding is held at medium confidence for this reason.

No runtime configuration confirming the agent's autonomy level was provided; autonomy is taken as declared behavior (direct single-turn reply, no spawning, no self-configuration) inferred from the prompt and runtime notes.
